message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.58,"fairness_assessment":"A ranked-choice or score vote fairly compares visibility, recruitment, equipment needs, and budget sufficiency without allowing the debate winner alone to determine the outcome. A transparent evidence-based scoring process is needed because each option has plausible but unverified benefits.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"Agent A","position":"Prioritizes a full inter-city tournament, buffet, and prizes to increase club visibility and recruit members.","influence":0.34},{"agent":"Agent B","position":"Prioritizes replacing worn educational equipment and purchasing teaching materials; this position won the debate with strong supporting quality.","influence":0.42},{"agent":"Agent C","position":"Supports an equal split between a smaller tournament and educational equipment to balance outreach and internal development.","influence":0.24}],"recommended_resolution":"collaborative","governance_reasoning":"Use a collaborative social-choice process: agree on evaluation criteria, verify the expected recruitment impact and the urgency of equipment replacement, then conduct a ranked or score vote among A, B, and C. A conditional or phased implementation can preserve flexibility, such as prioritizing essential equipment while reserving a smaller outreach budget if minimum funding thresholds are met."}
